note: The gate registry — the enumeration against which gate coverage is
An unregistered gate is the uncovered-by-default shape, so this file
is what makes a coverage claim mean anything: the number the check
prints is a fraction OF this list and of nothing else.
Deliberately NOT checks/registry.json, and the argument is mechanical
before it is philosophical: every entry there names a `file` that must
exist under checks/, and check-registry-conformance.sh fails any entry
that does not (checks/check-registry-conformance.sh:21-27). A gate is
not a file in checks/, so a gate row is a dangling entry by
construction. The admission record is check-loop economics too — tier,
runtime_ms, removal_signal — and a gate has no runtime and no loop
position. Merging would mean fabricating those fields or making them
optional, and an optional admission field is exactly the gap kogaki#6
was filed to close. Same coverage discipline, different admission

gates.raised_by: terrain/terrain.mjs gate + .claude/skills/terrain — the selection screen (specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md:76-86; kogaki#17)
gates.question: Which Strand does the article take as material?

options.label: Take no Strand from this survey; nothing is selected and the survey stands

gates.dynamic_options: Strand options are composed per run from the owner's current view (ids strand:<slug>, at most 3 beside the standing option — the selector affordance holds 4); the run's full declaration is written beside its capture in the machine-local run workspace, which never enters the tree (specs/SPEC.md §4 rider 3). Consulted 2026-08-05 (product-lab@16a6dbf6, two framings): no served position discriminates declaring a run-computed option set in a static registry — recorded as a miss, not resolved silently. The class is declared here, the content with the run; a capture that somehow reaches the tree and disagrees with this entry FAILS the options-equality check by design rather than being exempted.

gates.raised_by: terrain/terrain.mjs gate --proposal + .claude/skills/terrain — a rank/trim/hide proposal record presented for ratification (specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md:76-86; kogaki#17)
gates.question: The machine proposes narrowing the candidate set — apply it?

options.label: No narrowing; the full candidate set stands

gates.dynamic_options: The apply-option comes per run from the *.proposal.json record being presented (item 3's contract carries Where/Why/effect-stating label and the premise negation — the standing decline option here IS that negation, standing because the premise's negation is never optional). Same run-workspace siting and the same recorded consult miss as terrain-strand-selection. fork:false deliberately: Terrain attaches no recommendation to a trim — a ranked recommendation at this gate would be the machine narrowing twice, and the comparison obligation belongs to gates that genuinely fork.

gates.raised_by: terrain/terrain.mjs claim (subset path) + .claude/skills/terrain — a GroupClaim recomposed over a subset of the set it was pinned to, re-offered (specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md §7; kogaki#106, story 1.24)
gates.question: The group's members changed, so the claim was recomposed over the subset — which wording is adopted?

options.label: Keep the original wording; the recorded member set makes the mismatch legible rather than forbidden

gates.dynamic_options: The recomposed-claim option comes per run from the *.terrain-claim.json record being presented, whose `claim` was composed over the SUBSET the owner selected. The standing keep-original option is standing because §7 makes it explicitly available: a recomposed claim is a PROPOSAL, and the owner keeping the original wording over a changed member set is a legible mismatch rather than a forbidden one — the record carries the members, so the disagreement is readable rather than hidden. This gate exists because a change to the set a derived expression was derived from is a GATE EVENT rather than a refresh (topics/articles.md:73@f918c515); keeping the claim silently would assert commonality over absent members — a provenance lie — while discarding it would throw away the only thing in the interaction the machine did not supply. fork:false deliberately, for the same reason as terrain-trim-ratification: Terrain attaches no recommendation to which wording is truer over the subset, and a recommendation here would be the machine making the owner's judgment for them. Same run-workspace siting as the other two gates.

gates.raised_by: brief/brief.mjs enter + .claude/skills/brief — the thesis-determination gate (specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md §5.3 v9, kogaki#494; kogaki#488, story 1.72)
gates.question: Which Thesis does the Brief adopt?

options.label: The settled set is what should change — go back through Terrain and re-settle; no Brief is started and nothing is written (a Brief never fetches)

gates.dynamic_options: The 2-3 Thesis candidates are composed per run FROM THE SETTLED STRAND SET ONLY (§3's read-not-invented rule; ids thesis-1..thesis-3), each in plain register with its round-trip concession stated (SPEC-style-contract §4). The run's full declaration is written into the machine-local run state beside the composed candidates (pre-Thesis state is machine-local, §5.3 v9) — the same run-workspace siting as the terrain gates. The standing negation option is standing because the composing premise — this settled set supports a Thesis — is the machine's, and its negation routes back through Terrain, never a Brief fetch. fork:false deliberately: the runtime attaches no recommendation among its own candidates — ranking them would be the machine adopting a Thesis by another name, and the Thesis is the first piece of substantive OWNER judgment in the flow. The free-text answer becomes the adopted Thesis verbatim and does not discharge the negation option.

gates.raised_by: brief/brief.mjs adopt + .claude/skills/brief — the thesis-derived slug approval before the mint (specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md §5.3 v9, kogaki#494; kogaki#488, story 1.72)
gates.question: Approve the thesis-derived slug as the Brief's home name?

options.label: This Thesis should not name a Brief after all — reopen Thesis adoption; nothing is written under briefs/

gates.dynamic_options: Exactly ONE approve-option comes per run from the run state's slug_candidate — derived from the adopted Thesis, existing only after adoption (story 1.72 AC4), ordinary vocabulary and never a machine identity (SPEC-terrain §12.2's repair kept by the v9 route). The owner's free-form override IS the approved slug when given (lowercase-and-hyphens; the runtime's grammar refusal covers a malformed one). fork:false: one candidate plus an override is an approval, not a fork, and no recommendation is attached beyond the single derivation itself, which the option's label discloses. With no answer the mint never runs and nothing exists under briefs/ (story 1.72 AC6).
